item.aggregated_output: # Supplied workspace source/ contains the cleared editorial candidate from foculoom/aiartifacts. source-record.json records its exact bytes and base revision. existing-authoring/ is the already available skill-authoring workflow and scripts; inspect before use. official-sources/ contains inspected upstream contribution and installer documentation. Use the tools already available; no installation, external submission, publication or global configuration changes are authorized. Put requested artifacts under output/. # CLI reference [Back to the README](../README.md) Run commands with `npx skills `. For all available options, run `npx skills --help`. ## `skills add` Install skills from a repository, URL, or local directory: ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills ``` ### Source Formats ```bash # GitHub shorthand (owner/repo) npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills # Full GitHub URL npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills # Direct path to a skill in a repo npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/web-design-guidelines # GitLab URL npx skills add https://gitlab.com/org/repo # Azure Repos (Azure DevOps Services or Server) npx skills add https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo npx skills add https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo?path=/skills/web-design&version=GBmain # Any git URL npx skills add git@github.com:vercel-labs/agent-skills.git # Local path npx skills add ./my-local-skills ``` ### Private Repositories Use the same command for public and private repositories. The CLI uses the authentication already configured for the repository URL: ```bash # GitHub shorthand or HTTPS (Git credential helper, GitHub CLI, then SSH fallback) npx skills add acme/private-skills # SSH on GitHub, GitLab, or another Git host npx skills add git@github.com:acme/private-skills.git npx skills add ssh://git@git.example.com/acme/private-skills.git # HTTPS on any Git host (uses your configured Git credential helper) npx skills add https://git.example.com/acme/private-skills.git npx skills add https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/private-skills ``` For GitHub HTTPS and shorthand sources, `skills` first uses normal Git credentials. If that fails and GitHub CLI is authenticated, it tries `gh repo clone`, followed by SSH. It does not execute `gh auth token` or copy the stored GitHub CLI credential into the Node.js process. For GitHub tree lookups, `skills` first tries the API anonymously, then an explicitly supplied environment token, then `gh api`. GitHub CLI applies its own stored authentication and returns only the API response; the credential is never printed to or read by `skills`. If API access still fails, update checks fall back to an authenticated Git clone. `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` can be set explicitly for GitHub API access, including private repository downloads and update checks. They are optional for installs when Git, GitHub CLI, or SSH authentication is already configured. ### Options | Option | Description | | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `-g, --global` | Install to user directory instead of project | | `-a, --agent ` | Target specific agents (e.g., `claude-code`, `codex`). See [Supported Agents](agents.md#supported-agents) | | `-s, --skill ` | Install specific skills by name (use `'*'` for all skills) | | `-l, --list` | List available skills without installing | | `--copy` | Copy files instead of symlinking to agent directories | | `-y, --yes` | Skip all confirmation prompts | | `--all` | Install all skills to all agents without prompts | ### Examples ```bash # List skills in a repository npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --list # Install specific skills npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill frontend-design --skill skill-creator # Install a skill with spaces in the name (must be quoted) npx skills add owner/repo --skill "Convex Best Practices" # Install to specific agents npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills -a claude-code -a opencode # Non-interactive installation (CI/CD friendly) npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill frontend-design -g -a claude-code -y # Install all skills from a repo to all agents npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --all # Install all skills to specific agents npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill '*' -a claude-code # Install specific skills to all agents npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --agent '*' --skill frontend-design # Install from a direct SKILL.md or archive download URL npx skills add https://example.com/download/my-skill ``` Direct download URLs are tried after well-known discovery. They may point to a single valid `SKILL.md` file or a `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, or `.tgz` archive; the URL does not need to include a file extension. Downloads are limited to 10 MiB, extracted content to 25 MiB, and archives to 1000 files by default. Override with `SKILLS_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES`, `SKILLS_EXTRACT_MAX_BYTES`, and `SKILLS_EXTRACT_MAX_FILES` when you trust the source. ### Installation Scope | Scope | Flag | Location | Use Case | | ----------- | --------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | **Project** | (default) | `.//skills/` | Committed with your project, shared with team | | **Global** | `-g` | `~//skills/` | Available across all projects | ### Installation Methods When installing interactively, you can choose: | Method | Description | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Symlink** (Recommended) | Creates symlinks from each agent to a canonical copy. Single source of truth, easy updates. | | **Copy** | Creates independent copies for each agent. Use when symlinks aren't supported. | ## `skills use` Generate a prompt for one skill, or start a supported coding agent interactively: ```bash npx skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills@web-design-guidelines | claude npx skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines --agent claude-code ``` `skills use` resolves sources the same way as `skills add`, writes the selected skill files to a temporary directory, and prints only the generated prompt to stdout unless `--agent` is provided. With `--agent`, it starts one supported agent interactively with the generated prompt. ## `skills list` List all installed skills. Similar to `npm ls`. ```bash # List project installed skills npx skills list # List only global skills npx skills ls -g # Filter by specific agents npx skills ls -a claude-code -a cursor ``` ## `skills find` Search for skills interactively or by keyword. ```bash # Interactive search (fzf-style) npx skills find # Search by keyword npx skills find typescript # Search across every repository owned by an organization or user npx skills find react --owner vercel ``` ## `skills check` Check installed skills for available updates without reinstalling them: ```bash npx skills check ``` It exits with code 1 when any skill has an update, so it can gate CI. ## `skills update` ```bash # Update all skills (interactive scope prompt) npx skills update # Update a single skill by name npx skills update my-skill # Update multiple specific skills npx skills update frontend-design web-design-guidelines # Update only global or project skills npx skills update -g npx skills update -p # Non-interactive (auto-detects scope: project if in a project, else global) npx skills update -y ``` | Option | Description | | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `-g, --global` | Only update global skills | | `-p, --project` | Only update project skills | | `-y, --yes` | Skip scope prompt (auto-detect: project if in a project dir, else global) | | `[skills...]` | Update specific skills by name instead of all | ## `skills init` ```bash # Create SKILL.md in current directory npx skills init # Create a new skill in a subdirectory npx skills init my-skill ``` ## `skills remove` Remove installed skills from agents. ```bash # Remove interactively (select from installed skills) npx skills remove # Remove all skills from an exact lock source npx skills remove owner/repo # Remove specific skill by name npx skills remove web-design-guidelines # Remove multiple skills npx skills remove frontend-design web-design-guidelines # Remove from global scope npx skills remove --global web-design-guidelines # Remove from specific agents only npx skills remove --agent claude-code cursor my-skill # Remove all installed skills without confirmation npx skills remove --all # Remove all skills from a specific agent npx skills remove --skill '*' -a cursor # Remove a specific skill from all agents npx skills remove my-skill --agent '*' # Use 'rm' alias npx skills rm my-skill ``` | Option | Description | | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `-g, --global` | Remove from global scope (~/) instead of project | | `-a, --agent` | Remove from specific agents (use `'*'` for all) | | `-s, --skill` | Specify skills to remove (use `'*'` for all) | | `-y, --yes` | Skip confirmation prompts | | `--all` | Shorthand for `--skill '*' --agent '*' -y` | ## Experimental commands These commands are still experimental. Their names, options, and behavior may change. ### `skills experimental_sync` Sync skills from npm packages and `package.json` declarations. `sync` remains supported as a compatibility alias for users of skills@1.7.3. Install a package that ships skills, then sync them into your project: ```bash npm install -D skills agent-browser npx skills experimental_sync -y ``` Sync reads installed dependencies declared in your project's `package.json`, including `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, and `peerDependencies`. It discovers a package's root `SKILL.md`, `skills//SKILL.md`, or `dist/skills//SKILL.md` and links each skill into `.agents/skills/` and the selected agent directories. The linked skill updates with the installed package. Use `--copy` to copy files instead; copies require another sync after a package update. The `.agents/skills/` directory is the shared location. Selecting Claude Code also creates links under `.claude/skills/` pointing to the shared skills: ```bash npx skills experimental_sync -a claude-code -y ``` Outside an agent, sync detects installed agents. When run inside a coding agent, it targets that agent automatically unless you pass `-a` to select others. Already downloaded remote skills are reused to create missing agent links without fetching their source again. Packaged skills are relinked on every run. To run sync after dependency installation, add a `prepare` script: ```json { "scripts": { "prepare": "skills experimental_sync -y" } } ``` The project and its dependencies can also declare a `skills` array in `package.json`: ```json { "skills": ["npm:agent-browser", "vercel-labs/agent-skills@web-design-guidelines"] } ``` An `npm:` entry references skills in an installed package. Other entries reference Git sources and are fetched into the project. Pin a Git ref when you need reproducible remote content. A package can publish this array as a shareable skill pack. See the [field specification](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm/blob/main/SPEC.md) and [RFC](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/2323) for the full proposal. Sync tracks its skills in `skills-lock.json`, removes skills that are no longer provided, and preserves skills installed separately with `skills add`. When two skills share a name, sync applies these rules in order: 1. A skill installed with `skills add` is never shadowed, and a directory or link that sync did not create is never replaced. 2. A skill shipped by a direct dependency beats one from a transitive package, and a shipped skill beats one requested from a Git source. 3. Two packages at the same level shipping the same skill name install neither. Pick one with `--exclude #`. | Option | Description | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | `-a, --agent ` | Select agent directories | | `-y, --yes` | Skip confirmation prompts | | `--dry-run` | Show the plan without installing or removing skills | | `--copy` | Copy packaged skills instead of linking them | | `--no-cleanup` | Keep skills that are no longer provided | | `--no-remote` | Skip installing and removing remote skills | | `--include ` | Include skills by package or `package#skill` pattern | | `--exclude ` | Exclude skills by package or `package#skill` pattern | | `-r, --recursive` | Also read dependencies of workspace packages | | `--frozen-lockfile` | Fail instead of changing `skills-lock.json` (default in CI) | | `--no-frozen-lockfile` | Allow `skills-lock.json` to change in CI | The include/exclude filters apply to both packaged and remote skills. For remote skills, the package pattern matches the package declaring the entry (`.` for the project's own field). Eve always receives copies because it rewrites skill frontmatter. With `--frozen-lockfile`, sync installs only what `skills-lock.json` already records. It exits with code 1 and changes nothing when a packaged skill is missing from the lock, its content or package version differs, a locked skill is no longer provided by any dependency, or a remote `skills` entry resolves to different content. This is the default when a CI environment variable such as `CI` or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is set; pass `--no-frozen-lockfile` to update the lock from CI. ### Restore skills from the project lock file ```bash npx skills experimental_install ``` Restore supported sources recorded in `skills-lock.json` into `.agents/skills/`. Skills already in `.agents/skills/` are left as they are; pass `--force` to reinstall them. Entries from npm packages are synced from the dependencies already on disk, so install your npm dependencies before restoring. This command does not install npm packages or create agent-specific links for restored skills. | Option | Description | | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `--dry-run` | Show what would be restored without installing anything | | `--frozen-lockfile` | Fail instead of changing `skills-lock.json` (default in CI) | | `--no-frozen-lockfile` | Allow `skills-lock.json` to change in CI | | `--force` | Reinstall skills that are already in `.agents/skills/` | With `--frozen-lockfile`, every restored skill must match the content hash recorded in `skills-lock.json`. A source whose skills differ is skipped entirely, the lock is left untouched, and the command exits with code 1. A missing or empty lock is also an error. # Editorial-writing sharing candidate

Prepared 2026-10-30. **Ready for a reviewer decision; skills.sh installation and public discovery remain unverified.**

The self-contained candidate is `candidate/skills/editorial-writing/`, also bundled in `editorial-writing-candidate.zip` with the same `skills/editorial-writing/` layout. All 12 included files retain their source bytes, including canonical instructions, profiles, helper, tests, dependency notes and Apache-2.0 license. Only two generated `__pycache__/*.pyc` files were excluded. No plugin manifest, authoring toolkit, project prose or company planning records are bundled. No dependencies were installed, and no submission, publication, global configuration change or source edit was performed.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Supplied input and source-record SHA-256 checks | All matched before packaging; source and supplied inputs matched again at completion |
| Existing authoring `quick_validate.py` | Passed using already available PyYAML |
| Bundled checker tests, Python 3.9.6 and 3.12 | 27/27 passed on each with a physical temporary directory |
| Initial tests using macOS default temp path | Each had 3 failures and 2 errors: `/var` is a symlink, which the checker refuses to traverse |
| Relative Markdown file links | All 9 resolve inside the skill |
| Advisory prose checker on packaged Markdown | 9 files checked; no findings; no editorial-quality or authorship claim |
| Candidate file set, hashes and archive | Verified; no bytecode caches, symlinks or missing runtime resources |
| skills CLI / target-agent installation | Not run: standalone CLI unavailable; no installation authorized |
| Editorial behavior in a consuming agent | Not tested; static review and checker tests do not establish writing quality |

Raw results and logs are in `validation/`. `file-inventory.json` maps every source skill file to its packaged path or exclusion, with size and SHA-256. `source-inventory.json` covers the entire supplied `source/` tree, including the unchanged external plugin metadata. `SHA256SUMS` covers every output file except itself, relative to `output/`.

## Remaining work for the reviewer

1. Decide whether to share this unchanged Apache-2.0 candidate and confirm the selected public source/ref and applicable attribution/NOTICE requirements. No NOTICE file was supplied; no new copyright attribution or license was invented.
2. In an authorized distribution environment with a reviewed, pinned installer, verify discovery and an isolated installation for the intended agent. The supplied documentation supports the standard `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` layout, but this run did not execute the installer or confirm current upstream behavior.
3. Exercise representative adult web, longform, game UI/dialogue and early-reader requests in a consuming agent, including preservation of facts, placeholders and deliberate repetition. These are future behavioral checks, not completed acceptance tests.
4. Accept or separately address the existing symlink-ancestor restriction: normal macOS `/var` and `/tmp` aliases can cause optional lint to reject an input. Canonical physical paths work; this package preserves the checker unchanged.

This candidate exists only as local review artifacts as of 2026-10-30. This task did not establish public acquisition, a skills.sh listing, installation counts or existing upstream public availability. Any later sharing action requires separate authorization.
# Dependencies and provenance

## Source and transformation

Supplied source: `https://github.com/foculoom/aiartifacts`, revision `211ad9da8b7a3d0740d1896a74c018ed3ad097be`, path `plugins/editorial/skills/editorial-writing`. This is supplied provenance, verified against local recorded hashes, not an independently fetched remote revision. The workspace README identifies this as the cleared editorial candidate.

The copied `SKILL.md` declares `Apache-2.0`; the full supplied `LICENSE` and `DEPENDENCIES.md` are retained verbatim. No relicensing or instruction edits were made. The source's dependency notes identify the profiles, synthetic examples and helper as Foculoom-authored and state that no third-party prose/code is vendored. That statement is recorded provenance, not an independent rights audit. The source plugin manifest corroborates the Apache-2.0 declaration but is context only, not required by this standalone skill and not copied into the candidate.

`file-inventory.json` records the two excluded generated CPython 3.12 caches alongside every retained file. Exclusion removes interpreter-specific artifacts, without changing executable source or tests. `source-inventory.json` records all source files for the no-edit check. SHA-256 detects byte changes; it is not a publisher signature.

| Instructions and profiles | Agent Skills-compatible host able to read local files | All references included; actual host behavior untested |
| Advisory prose checker | Optional Python 3.9+, standard library only | Included unchanged; exercised on Python 3.9.6 and 3.12 |

| skills CLI / distribution tooling | Separate reviewed, pinned development dependency | Not installed or executed; `npx` availability was not treated as CLI availability |

No external skill, MCP server, SDK, credential, network service or package-manager installation is required by the packaged helper. The host's model and filesystem facilities remain host requirements. Existing authoring tools are development tools, not skill runtime dependencies. No initializer was run because this is an existing skill; optional UI metadata was not added.

Used the supplied `existing-authoring/SKILL.md` workflow and inspected `scripts/quick_validate.py` before running it. The workflow favors preserving task scope, retaining relevant resources and validating existing skills without reinitializing them.

Distribution conclusions use supplied upstream snapshots, not live skills.sh verification:

- `official-sources/skills-creating.md`: repository discovery includes `skills/`; skill frontmatter requires `name` and `description`.
- `official-sources/skills-commands.md`: supports local source directories and a listing option. No command was run to download or install the CLI.

# Creating skills

[Back to the README](../README.md)

Create a template with `npx skills init my-skill`, then edit its `SKILL.md`.

Skills are directories containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill
description: What this skill does and when to use it
---

# My Skill

Instructions for the agent to follow when this skill is activated.

## When to Use

Describe the scenarios where this skill should be used.

## Steps

1. First, do this
2. Then, do that
```

### Required Fields

- `name`: Unique identifier (lowercase, hyphens allowed)
- `description`: Brief explanation of what the skill does

### Optional Fields

- `metadata.internal`: Set to `true` to hide the skill from normal discovery. Internal skills are only visible and
  installable when `INSTALL_INTERNAL_SKILLS=1` is set. Useful for work-in-progress skills or skills meant only for
  internal tooling.

```markdown
---
name: my-internal-skill
description: An internal skill not shown by default
metadata:
  internal: true
---
```

### Skill Discovery

The CLI searches for skills in these locations within a repository. Each
skill container directory is walked up to three levels deep, covering flat
layouts (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) and catalog layouts with one or two category
levels (`skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md` or
`skills/<category>/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md`). A `SKILL.md` discovered at a
shallower level shadows anything nested below it. Use `--full-depth` to also
discover `SKILL.md` files outside these container directories (e.g. under
`examples/` or `tests/`).

<!-- skill-discovery:start -->
- Root directory (if it contains `SKILL.md`)

### Plugin Manifest Discovery

If `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` or `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` exists, skills declared in those files are also discovered:

```json
// .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
{
  "metadata": { "pluginRoot": "./plugins" },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "my-plugin",
      "source": "my-plugin",
      "skills": ["./skills/review", "./skills/test"]
    }
  ]
}
```

This enables compatibility with the [Claude Code plugin marketplace](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces) ecosystem. Skill paths declared in a manifest are searched at their declared depth and are not subject to the bounded depth-3 catalog walk described above.

### Custom Discovery Paths

If your skills live somewhere else, list those directories in the `paths` field of a `skills.sh.json` file at the repository root:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://skills.sh/schemas/skills.sh.schema.json",
  "paths": ["./tools/skills"]
}
```

Each entry is a container directory. Its subdirectories are searched the same way as `skills/`, up to three levels deep. Entries must start with `./` and point to a subdirectory of the repository; any other entries, including the repository root itself, are ignored. The CLI searches these directories along with the standard locations above. If two skills have the same name, only the first one found is kept.

If no skills are found in standard locations, a recursive search is performed.
